resources.public_interpretation: All three runs completed the same 200-node, 50-step workload, 10 checks and checksum 21144 with identical geometry. Compared with accepted 226, 234 fixed-work CPU increased 0.019637 CPU-seconds (7.27%) over approximately 4.00 seconds of matched fully covered intervals; late-idle CPU increased 0.009958 seconds. Sampled whole-window RSS/PSS were 1.859/2.130 MiB lower. No predeclared material-regression investigation threshold was reached, and no repeat was warranted. These single-run measurements neither prove an optimization nor measure throughput. Chromium browser-only memory is descriptive and separate from ChromeDriver.

limitations: The640-file campaign is a fixed non-URL sample, not the whole WPT repository. Native, assertion, rendering and authored-control denominators remain separate.
Dedicated URL conformance work remains deferred as requested; three named native URL targets are excluded.
Five checkVisibility upstream assertions remain failing; content-visibility:auto, unassigned-slot box behavior and listbox option boxes are not completed.
Hidden content retains layout/style data for correctness. No layout/style-skipping optimization or full content-visibility conformance is claimed.
Lifecycle and hidden-scroll comparisons retain the explicitly listed observable scheduling/geometry distinctions.
General CSS cascade layer/origin rollback, complete grid/multicol layout, document.domain and iframe realm/async-loading work remain outside this repair.
The reference adapter does not expose Chromium's OS exit status; it records its own successful completion and task-owned profile/process cleanup.
Resource values are sampled and workload-specific; the paced fixture does not measure throughput or general browser speed.
The executable is the tested Linux development build with external dependencies; it is not a portable standalone package.
All650 exported build inputs and reviewed extras match the tested source. No fresh hermetic rebuild or byte-reproducible compiler claim is made.
Public source and Git bundle contain only reviewed public ancestry; private task history, authentication, profiles and capture machinery are excluded.
